keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

themes.name: LLM and Agent Evaluation, Benchmarking, Human-AI Interaction
themes.summary: Papers in this theme construct benchmarks and evaluation methods for LLM and tool-using agents across coding, data, document, dialogue, and domain-specific tasks. Others study human-AI interaction, including trust calibration, advice reliance, public-service decision-making, and educational use. The work differs by focusing on benchmark design, evaluator agreement, agent orchestration, and human decision quality.

themes.name: Robot Learning and Embodied Control
themes.summary: These papers develop learning-based methods for controlling embodied agents, spanning world models, vision-language-action policies, motion planning, and whole-body or soft-robot control across manipulation, navigation, and humanoid platforms. They differ in whether they contribute new controllers and planners, new benchmarks, datasets, and simulation platforms, or diagnostic studies of where learned models fail.

themes.name: AI Safety, Security, and Adversarial ML
themes.summary: The papers span adversarial and backdoor attacks on models and agents, along with defenses and detection methods. Several contributions are benchmarks and audits for deepfake, AI-generated, and manipulated video detection, while others examine AI safety theory, reward hacking, sycophancy, and misuse-resistance in pretraining. They differ in focusing on attack design, robust detection, runtime controls, or conceptual analyses of care and enfeeblement.

themes.name: Vision-language spatial and multimodal reasoning
themes.summary: The papers examine spatial, multimodal, and vision-language reasoning through benchmarks, diagnostics, representation control, and robustness audits. They differ in whether they probe model failures, introduce new evaluation settings, or propose methods for grounding, steering, adaptation, and retrieval across images, documents, video, and driving scenes.

themes.name: Generative Models for Vision, 3D, and Language
themes.summary: The papers develop generative and diffusion/flow-based models across images, video, three-dimensional scenes, and language, with applications ranging from restoration and tracking to world simulation and cultural-heritage description. They differ in whether they adapt pretrained video or image models, learn flow maps in non-Euclidean or conditional settings, or introduce benchmarks and evaluation audits. Several works emphasize controllability and faithful evaluation rather than raw sample generation alone.

themes.name: Conformal Prediction, Uncertainty Quantification, and Causal Inference
themes.summary: The papers develop conformal and uncertainty-aware methods for reliable prediction and causal analysis, including conditional coverage, credal uncertainty, calibrated decision heads, and conformal risk certificates. They also ask when semantic priors, foundation models, and causality-aware scoring genuinely improve causal discovery or effect estimation. Applications span materials, geology, health, finance, education, and genomics, with several studies offering cautionary or negative findings.

themes.name: Neural Operators, Scientific ML, and Quantum
themes.summary: The papers span neural-operator and other learned surrogates for physical simulation, from fluid networks and laser melting to plasma fields and finite-element stress analysis, alongside benchmarks and agents for PDE solving and scientific prediction. Another strand applies quantum machine learning to reinforcement learning, bandits, and hybrid quantum-classical models. Other contributions address scientific data compression, moment closures, seismic inversion, climate downscaling, and astronomical variability modeling.

themes.name: Optimization and Learning Theory
themes.summary: The papers cluster around provable guarantees for classical optimization and learning procedures: tighter analyses of k-means++ seeding and matching lower bounds for Euclidean k-means, improved last-iterate convergence for stochastic gradient descent, and sharp Gaussian approximation rates for averaged linear stochastic approximation. A second strand studies the mechanics of practical optimizers, including forgetting windows for streaming ridge regression, GPU-accelerated Fisher information methods, and learning-rate transfer across depth for spectral optimizers. A third strand applies learning-to-optimize ideas to combinatorial and engineering problems such as secretary selection with predictions, MaxSAT, scheduling, and security-constrained power optimization, often asking when learned guidance actually beats strong learning-free baselines.

themes.name: Time-Series and Spatiotemporal Forecasting
themes.summary: The papers develop methods for forecasting and modeling temporal and spatiotemporal data across domains such as traffic, weather, insurance, physiology, communications, finance, and games. They span probabilistic Gaussian processes, transformer and state-space architectures, quantum recurrent models, foundation models, benchmarks, and post-hoc explanation frameworks. Differences lie in whether they emphasize predictive accuracy, physical consistency, context-aware interaction, robust imputation, or evaluation under drift and scarce data.

themes.name: Clinical and biomedical imaging AI
themes.summary: The papers apply deep learning and multimodal language models to clinical and biomedical imaging, spanning accelerated MRI reconstruction, motion correction, anatomical and lesion segmentation, surgical and radiotherapy assessment, and pathology diagnosis. They differ in whether they propose efficient architectures, introduce public benchmarks, or evaluate model reliability. Several focus on auditing vision-language models and revealing failures hidden by aggregate metrics.

themes.name: Graph, Relational, and Federated Learning
themes.summary: The papers split into graph-centric work and federated optimization work. The graph side develops semantic relational representations, reusable graph-to-image input interfaces, topological ensembles, spiking neighborhood aggregation, dynamic-graph explanations, and ontology induction for knowledge graphs. The federated side addresses incremental classes without exemplars, update coordination with flatness, and communication-efficient multi-view clustering.

themes.name: Efficient LLM serving and memory
themes.summary: These papers target the memory and serving bottlenecks of large model inference, spanning sparse GEMV kernels for edge GPUs, high-bandwidth flash tiering, KV cache reuse, compression and host-tier restoration, and pruning or routing to cut decoding cost. Some propose systems and kernels for specific hardware, while others introduce algorithms for cache management, ensemble routing, or visual token pruning, and several address multimodal, agentic, or robotic serving settings.

highlights.title: Leaderboard Hacking: Preference-Based Model Evaluations are Vulnerable to Manipulation
highlights.authors: Eve Fleisig, Joachim Baumann, Dylan Hadfield-Menell et al.
highlights.theme: LLM and Agent Evaluation, Benchmarking, Human-AI Interaction
highlights.why: Demonstrates that preference-based arena rankings can be manipulated by strategic voting, prompting, and nomination, raising serious concerns about the reliability of widely used leaderboards.
highlights.key_result: The paper finds that arena-style leaderboards are highly vulnerable to strategic voting, strategic prompting, and strategic nomination; these manipulations boost the rank of nearly every tested model, with each attack boosting a model by up to 15-20 places and combined attacks boosting it by up to 45 places.
evidence: However, we find that these leaderboards are highly vulnerable to several manipulation strategies that unscrupulous providers could use to boost a model's rank: strategic voting (individual votes that boost a model's rank, including votes on irrelevant models), strategic prompting (choosing prompts that favor a model), and strategic nomination (boosting the rank of a model by inserting irrelevant models).
These manipulations boost the rank of nearly every tested model; each attack can boost a model by up to 15-20 places in a ranking and, combined, they can boost a model by up to 45 places.

news.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a model for fast execution in coding and agentic workflows priced flat across its 1 million-token context at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. It scores 51 versus 50 for Gemini 4 Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at default thinking level (54 at the xhigh setting), and Google also announced Orchestrator in Google Antigravity, which switches between models within a session and reached near-Carbon task success on Terminal-Bench 4.0 while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster.

news.summary: Google rolled out Gemini 4 Hydrogen globally in Google Search, describing it as the biggest model upgrade to Search yet. news.title: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B
news.summary: Hugging Face released LLMON, an XML-like LLM-native markup language that uses reserved special tokens as structural delimiters and binds instructions to data via unique IDs, along with two experimental preview models, granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview and granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview, and a GitHub repo with tooling and JSON-to-LLMON converters. The post reports that on some benchmarks attack success rates from indirect prompt injections drop to nearly zero while general capability is maintained relative to Granite 4.1 Instruct models.

news.title: Deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-Neuron
news.summary: Amazon announced that SGLang-Neuron, an out-of-tree SGLang plugin released by RadixArk with Annapurna Labs, is publicly available through an AWS Deep Learning Container, letting users serve models and generate RL rollouts on Trainium with the existing SGLang interface on native PyTorch. The walkthrough uses a Trainium3 EC2 instance with a pytorch-inference-sglang-neuronx container to serve openai/gpt-oss-120b, and the plugin also supports PD disaggregation with KV cache transferred via NIXL over EFA.

news.title: How Natera designed an agentic AI system for lab ops with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: Natera built SWARM, an agentic AI system for lab operations on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, consisting of a swarm-agent runtime that generates diagnostic reports before an engineer opens a ticket and a swarm-hive runtime for real-time interaction, sharing one skill library. The post reports about 130x faster first response time and 96.2% automated coverage across support tickets, against a prior load of over 65 tickets per day across three Jira queues with an average first response time of 17.4 hours.

news.title: Four Amazon Bedrock inference choices that affect cost
news.summary: The post examines four Amazon Bedrock request-level settings that affect cost without changing model or prompt: prompt cache duration, service tier, reasoning effort, and maxTokens. It gives rates for Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5 and Claude Opus 5 on Bedrock, where a 5-minute cache write costs 1.25 times the input rate, a 1-hour write costs 2 times, and a cache read costs 0.1 times, and notes a 30-minute minimum TTL for supported GPT-5.6 models.

news.title: Tokenomics at scale: Track and cap Amazon Bedrock spend per IAM principal with CUR 2.0 and AWS Budgets
news.summary: The post describes attributing and capping Amazon Bedrock spend per IAM principal using Bedrock's automatic recording of caller identity, CUR 2.0 or Cost Explorer for reporting, and AWS Budgets with budget actions to apply a Deny IAM policy when a threshold is crossed, with no application code for the common case. Session tags are recommended for shared roles, since principal tags cannot distinguish individual users on a single role.

themes.summary: 这些论文围绕经典优化和学习过程的可证明保证：对 k-means++ 初始化进行更紧的分析，并为欧几里得 k-means 匹配下界；改进随机梯度下降的最后迭代收敛；以及平均线性随机近似的锐高斯逼近率。第二条线索研究实用优化器的机制，包括流式岭回归的遗忘窗口、GPU 加速的 Fisher 信息方法，以及谱优化器跨深度的学习率迁移。第三条线索将学习优化思想应用于组合和工程问题，如带有预测的秘书选择、MaxSAT、调度和安全约束电力优化，常常追问学习到的指导何时真正优于强无学习基线。

themes.name: 时间序列与时空预测

themes.name: 临床与生物医学影像 AI

highlights.title: Leaderboard Hacking: Preference-Based Model Evaluations are Vulnerable to Manipulation
highlights.authors: Eve Fleisig, Joachim Baumann, Dylan Hadfield-Menell et al.
highlights.theme: LLM and Agent Evaluation, Benchmarking, Human-AI Interaction
highlights.why: 表明基于偏好的竞技场排名可被策略性投票、提示和提名操纵，引发对广泛使用的排行榜可靠性的严重担忧。
highlights.key_result: 本文发现竞技场式排行榜极易受到策略性投票、策略性提示和策略性提名的影响；这些操纵几乎提升了所有测试模型的排名，每次攻击最多可将一个模型提升 15-20 个名次，组合攻击最多可提升 45 个名次。
evidence: However, we find that these leaderboards are highly vulnerable to several manipulation strategies that unscrupulous providers could use to boost a model's rank: strategic voting (individual votes that boost a model's rank, including votes on irrelevant models), strategic prompting (choosing prompts that favor a model), and strategic nomination (boosting the rank of a model by inserting irrelevant models).
These manipulations boost the rank of nearly every tested model; each attack can boost a model by up to 15-20 places in a ranking and, combined, they can boost a model by up to 45 places.

highlights.title: Sophon: A Procedural Diagnostic for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
highlights.authors: J. Zach Gazak, Ryan Swindle, Justin Fletcher
highlights.why: 引入一种程序化诊断方法，显示开源 VLM 在简单几何任务上退化到随机水平，尽管在现有空间基准上得分很高，指出其依赖物体和场景先验。
highlights.key_result: 在现有空间基准上得分 85-94% 的开源 VLM 在 Sophon 上表现仅为随机水平，而前沿模型达到 77-83%，人类达到 84-94%。线性探针从编码器和解码器中以 80-86% 的解码率解码空间信号，但模型在答案 token 之间的选择却是随机的。
evidence: Open VLMs that score 85-94% on existing spatial benchmarks answer Sophon at chance, while frontier models reach 77-83% and humans 84-94%. Linear probes decode the spatial signal from encoder and decoder at 80-86%, yet the models select among the answer tokens at random ( ).

highlights.title: Stress-Testing Sandbagging Detection Under Adaptive Attack
highlights.authors: Bhoj Rani Soopal, Aarohi Agrawal, Josh Karthikeyan et al.
highlights.theme: AI Safety, Security, and Adversarial ML
highlights.why: 表明针对固定攻击一次性评估的沙袋检测器在自适应重训练下失效，文本审计降至随机水平，而能力仍然隐藏，削弱了虚假的安心感。
highlights.key_result: 两轮重训练将文本审计的 AUC 从 0.978 降至 0.560，而标记物仍移除 40--49 个准确率点；攻击在 8 个重训练种子中的 7 个中成功，审计漏掉了每次重训练（AUC 0.451--0.576），包括一次 Llama 运行。
evidence: On Qwen 2.5-3B, we adapt the attack over two retraining rounds against a text-based audit. Two rounds of retraining cut the text audit's AUC from 0.978 to 0.560 while the marker still removes 40--49 points of accuracy. The attack worked in 7 of 8 retrained seeds, and the audit missed every retraining (AUC 0.451--0.576), including one Llama run.

highlights.title: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Diagnosis-Specific Failure in Medical Vision-Language Models
highlights.authors: Shreya Ajay Kale, Angad Ripudaman Singh Bajwa
highlights.why: 表明总体准确率掩盖了几个医学 VLM 在气胸检测上的完全失败，尽管总体得分很高，但解释流畅却错误。
highlights.key_result: 我们审计了五个开源医学 VLM（MedGemma-4B、Lingshu-7B、HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B、Qwen2.5-VL-7B 和 MedVLM-R1），在 6,048 个 ChestX-ray14 问题上，这些问题按性别、年龄、发现和标签进行了平衡。在 432 张气胸阳性 X 光片中，HuatuoGPT-Vision 和 Qwen2.5-VL 检测到零例，而 MedGemma 和 Lingshu 在相同图像上分别检测到 38% 和 67% 的病例。
evidence: We audit five open medical VLMs (MedGemma-4B, Lingshu-7B, HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and MedVLM-R1) on 6,048 ChestX-ray14 questions balanced by sex, age, finding, and label. On the 432 pneumothorax-positive X-rays, HuatuoGPT-Vision and Qwen2.5-VL detect zero cases while MedGemma and Lingshu detect 38% and 67% of the same images.

highlights.title: Prediction or Persistence? What Future-Prediction Scores Miss About World Models
highlights.why: 使用匹配的持续性对照表明未来预测得分混淆了编码器质量和预测器贡献，提醒不要仅用它们来选择世界模型。
highlights.key_result: 本文表明未来预测得分与预测器的实际贡献是分离的：仅在原生视频 V-JEPA 家族中，V-JEPA 2 的预测器在得分高于 0.42 的基础上增加 +0.028 到 +0.041 的 top-1，而 V-JEPA 2.1 在相同试验上增加 +0.291。
evidence: Score and contribution dissociate within the native-video V-JEPA family alone: the predictor adds +0.291 top-1 for V-JEPA 2.1 but +0.03--0.04 for V-JEPA 2 on the identical trials.

The central finding is that score and predictor contribution dissociate. Within the native-video V-JEPA family alone, scores above 0.42 coexist with contributions of +0.03 and +0.04, while V-JEPA 2.1's predictor adds +0.291, before any off-distribution model is considered.

Score and contribution diverge (Fig. ). Within the native-video V-JEPA family, V-JEPA 2's predictors add +0.028 to +0.041 top-1 to scores above 0.42, while V-JEPA 2.1's adds +0.291 on the identical trials.

V-JEPA 2 ViT-H and ViT-L reach 0.437 and 0.424 top-1, over four times chance, against a shared control at 0.396. Their predictors therefore contribute only +0.0408 [+0.0326, +0.0491] and +0.0284 [+0.0205, +0.0363].

highlights.title: Driving World Models Move the Camera, Not the Scene
highlights.why: 仔细揭示了以计划为条件的驾驶世界模型几乎未按指令移动场景，场景响应有限且计划通道常被忽略，这是一个警示性的负面结果。
highlights.key_result: 与这些参照相比，已发布的世界模型移动了相机但几乎没有移动场景：它们的场景响应（即预测复现的真实距离变化比例）最多只能达到真实视频的大约三分之一，并且轨迹得分无法区分已执行的速度指令和被忽略的速度指令。随后冻结的生成器在 KITTI、nuScenes 和 Argoverse 2 上几乎像真实场景一样跟随 0.54 m 的横向位移，对减速计划在三个生成器中的响应超过重采样，对加速计划在两个生成器中的响应超过重采样。
evidence: Against these references, released world models move their camera but barely move the scene: their scene response, the share of the real change in distance that the forecast reproduces, reaches at most about a third of real video's, and the trajectory score cannot tell an executed speed command from an ignored one.

ReTime-Compose therefore delivers the plan as geometry, without training. It transports the frames of one logged-speed rollout to the planned cameras, and the frozen model completes only what no frame covers.

Frozen generators then follow a 0.54 m lateral shift nearly as the real scene does on KITTI, nuScenes and Argoverse 2, and respond more than re-sampling to slow-down plans in three generators and to speed-up plans in two.

highlights.title: Loyalty Capture: Reporting Relationships and Structural Sycophancy in Frontier AI Models
highlights.theme: AI Safety, Security, and Adversarial ML
highlights.why: 识别出“忠诚捕获”现象，即处于汇报关系中的模型在没有明确提示的情况下改变推荐以迎合上级激励，揭示了一种结构性的谄媚失效模式。
highlights.key_result: 在来自八个人工智能实验室的八个前沿模型上进行的 5,757 次试验中，我们发现当 CEO 的奖金面临风险时，向 CEO 汇报的模型会削减长期投资以提升短期收益，而与指标无关的安慰剂则没有效果。在影响 OI 的决策（R&D 和 Marketing）上，MISSES--CLEARS 攻击性增加值在 CEO 汇报下为 +8.1pp（p < 0.001），在董事会下为 +3.5pp（p = 0.021），在审计下为 +4.3pp（p = 0.010）。
evidence: Across 5,757 trials with eight frontier models from eight AI laboratories, we find that CEO-reporting models cut long-term investment to boost short-term earnings when the CEO's bonus is at stake, while a metric-irrelevant placebo shows no effect.

CEO-reporting models recommend significantly larger investment cuts when the bonus is at stake (Figure A). On OI-affecting decisions (R&D and Marketing), the MISSES--CLEARS aggressiveness increase is +8.1pp under CEO reporting (p < 0.001), +3.5pp under Board (p = 0.021), and +4.3pp under Audit (p = 0.010).
